channel.title: France 24 - International breaking news, top stories and headlines
channel.description: Breaking news and world news from France 24 on Business, Sports, Culture. Video news. News from the US, Europe, Asia Pacific, Africa, Middle East, America

item.title: Trump says US-Iran talks continue, warns Tehran faces 'last chance'
item.description: The US president insisted negotiations were underway despite Tehran's denials, saying Iran had a final opportunity to reach an agreement on the Strait of Hormuz and its nuclear programme before facing what he called 'decapitation.'
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Hundreds flee Tigray after fighting flares near border
item.description: In tonight's edition, hundreds of people run from the most serious fighting to break out in Tigray since 2022. Also, Nigeria's still probing links that Mexican drug cartels may have to Africa's top economy. And Cape Verde’s veteran goalkeeper ⁠Vozinha arrived in Chile ​to join first division club Colo-Colo.
item.dc:creator: Georja CALVIN-SMITH

item.title: Europe's record-breaking heat sparks wildfires, drought in France, Greece and the UK
item.description: Europe's record-breaking hot and dry summer continues to take its toll on France and Greece, where firefighters fought to contain major blazes, while the UK recorded its driest July in nearly two centuries. Europe is Earth’s fastest-warming continent, heating at more than twice the global average since the 1980s, according to the European Union’s Copernicus climate service.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Norway's Haugset wins stage 3 to claim Tour de France Femmes lead
item.description: Norway's Sigrid Haugset won stage three of the Women's Tour de France on Monday, seizing the overall lead and yellow jersey from Dutch rider Lorena Wiebes. Haugset launched a gutsy solo attack less than halfway into the hilly 156.6km route between Geneva and Poligny, and held off Belgium's Lotte Kopecky.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: France: Water sports enthusiasts 'fly' above the River Seine
item.description: Parisians are defying gravity on the Seine thanks to the e-foil, an electric board equipped with a propeller. The board emerges from the water as soon as it gains speed, creating the feeling of flying just above the surface.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Ceuta migrant influx reignites immigration divisions in Europe
item.description: The arrival of 60,000 people into the Spanish North African enclave of Ceuta from Morocco last week has created serious tensions within the EU over immigration. Spain has called for a meeting of EU interior ministers which is due to take place Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Bridge collapse in DR Congo reignites debate about mining revenues
item.description: Several people ended up in the river after an important bridge collapsed on June 3 in the village of Hombo in the eastern part of the DRC. The bridge is one of the failing critical infrastructures in a territory that is home to one of the most lucrative mines in the region.
item.dc:creator: The FRANCE 24 Observers

item.title: "The situation is out of control": Greek firefighters battle wildfire for fourth day
item.description: Greek firefighters are battling a wildfire northwest of Athens for the fourth day, as strong and erratic winds continue to fan the blaze. Fires throughout the country have killed five firefighters since last week.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Across the EU, immigration being used as a 'political tool' across the political spectrum
item.description: Delano D'Souza is pleased to welcome Dr. Manlio Graziano, Founder and Director of Nicholas Spykman International Center for Geopolitical Analysis. Italy's temporary suspension of the Schengen Agreement with Spain, following the migration episode in Ceuta, is presented less as a meaningful European policy than as a symbolic act driven by domestic politics. Dr Graziano argues that the episode reveals how migration has become an instrument of political positioning rather than policy making. His analysis suggests that Giorgia Meloni's principal audience is not Brussels or Madrid, but Italy's increasingly fragmented right, where competition from parties positioned even further to her right is compelling her to continually reaffirm her hardline credentials.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: EU calls for 'united action' on border protection after Ceuta mass crossing
item.description: The European Commission President, Ursula Von der Leyen, has reiterated the EU's support to help tackle illegal migration following last week's chaos in the Spanish enclave of Ceuta in North Africa. The crisis has fanned anti-immigrant rhetoric by right wing politicians in Europe and sparked diplomatic tensions between Spain and some EU members, notably Italy. An emergency video conference of EU interior ministers is due to be held on August 3, on Rome's call.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Myanmar: Ousted leader Suu Kyi makes rare appearance with Red Cross representative
item.description: Former leader Aung San Suu Kyi met with an representative of the International Committee of the Red Cross on August 3rd. The 81-year-old Nobel Peace Prize winner was taken into detention in early 2021, when a military coup ousted her elected civilian government. Since then, her location and condition have been largely unknown to international officials and the public.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Anti-war politician and Kremlin critic Boris Nadezhdin flees Russia for France
item.description: Kremlin critic and anti-war politician Boris Nadezhdin – who openly criticised President Vladimir Putin and Moscow's Ukraine offensive – said Monday he had fled Russia for Paris. Nadezhdin was recently detained outside Moscow and blocked from running for parliament. Russia's clampdown on dissent has left most critics in jail, in exile or dead.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Iran 'calls Trump's bluff' as it denies negotiating with the US
item.description: U.S. President Donald Trump said new talks to wind down the war in Iran will start on August 3, after announcing he is holding off on new massive strikes he had threatened to unleash on the country. This is not a one-time occurrence: Trump has regularly announced ongoing talks after threatening agressive strikes on Iran. But this time, Iran seems to not have given into the strategy. FRANCE 24's Kethevane Gorjestani tells us more.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: France slams hard-right Reform UK party's plan to use navy to stop Channel migrants
item.description: The hard-right Reform UK party on Monday revealed plans for "the largest military operation" in the Channel "since World War II", which would deploy Britain's Royal Navy to return small migrant boats to France. France was quick to slam the proposal later on Monday, calling it "a violation of French sovereignty".
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: After Donald Trump's latest U-turn, uncertainty remains over talks with Iran
item.description: Between the U-turns, the posturing, the denials and the flexing of military might, it's hard to know exactly where negotiations between the US and Iran are actually at - if they have gone anywhere. While US President Donald Trump says negotiations are underway, Tehran has denied that any are planned but that it is in talks with Oman.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Amid a drought and soaring temperatures, Hungary shuts down its nuclear plant
item.description: Nuclear power is often touted as a solution to global warming. It comes with risks, but creates energy without the same greenhouse gas emissions as coal or gas plants. However, rising temperatures and drought in Europe are creating problems and shutdowns at nuclear power plants. With water levels too low to cool the reactors, Hungary - for example - is shutting down the reactor that's meant to provide energy for half the country.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Ceuta migrant crisis: Far-right govts 'ridiculously using these images' to stoke fear for votes
item.description: Jennie Shin is pleased to welcome Antoni Vives, policy analyst and the former Deputy Mayor of Barcelona. Vives offers a nuanced geopolitical interpretation of the Ceuta migration crisis, arguing that the events cannot be understood solely as a humanitarian emergency or a spontaneous wave of migration. Vives frames the crisis within a broader framework encompassing historical colonial legacies, demographic and economic inequalities, regional power competition between Morocco and Algeria, and the strategic use of migration as an instrument of statecraft. While acknowledging the aspirations of young Moroccans seeking economic opportunity, he contends that the scale and timing of the crossings reflect deliberate geopolitical signalling by Morocco toward Spain.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Trump's Board of Peace reassures Israel after objections on Gaza pullout plan
item.description: US President Donald Trump's postwar transition body The Board of Peace on Monday assured Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu that Israel's withdrawal would only begin after Hamas's complete disarmament, following objections. Israel had objected to the board's Thursday text that called for a phased withdrawal within the territory and the immediate cessation of Israeli strikes in Gaza.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Ceuta: Parents gather at Moroccan border, desperate for news of their children
item.description: In the Moroccan town of Fnideq, parents are gathering along the border fence, waiting for news of their children. On July 30 and 31, over 60,000 migrants crossed the border to the Spanish enclave of Ceuta.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: 'Spain expects solidarity' as it grapples with aftermath of Ceuta migration surge
item.description:
Most of the estimated 60,000 people who rushed into Ceuta have returned to Morocco since the territory's largest mass migrant crossing. Spanish authorities reported at least 72 deaths on August 2.
France 24 asked Juan Fernando Lopez Aguilar, former Spanish Justice Minister and current MEP, constitutional law professor, and jurist from the Spanish Socialist Workers’ Party how Ceuta is reckoning with the aftermath of the border surge.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Cuba could collapse. Here’s what Trump wants.
item.description:
After Venezuela and Iran, could Cuba be Donald Trump’s next target?
As the island endures its worst crisis in decades, Washington is hardening its stance and imposing further sanctions.
Is this merely political posturing, or part of a genuine strategy by the US president? How far are the United States prepared to go?
In this video, France 24's Stella Elgersma, together with several experts, examines the geopolitical stakes and the possible scenarios surrounding the communist island, to understand what is unfolding just 90 miles off the coast of the United States.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: After the fires, France's touristy southwest reckons with their economic fallout
item.description: With one of the worst wildfires in French history gradually being brought under control in southwestern Gironde region, life is slowly returning. In summertime, that means tourism - holidaymakers are trying to get their plans back on track as hotels and campsites reopen. But for the businesses that rely on vacationers, it will be a long road to recovery, with the already record fire season still not over.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: French court rejects pro-Kremlin commentator's expulsion appeal
item.description: A Paris court on Monday rejected an appeal by a Russian television commentator Xenia Fedorova against an order to leave France after authorities accused her of spreading pro-Kremlin propaganda.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Infantino's grip on FIFA weakened following investor plan controversy
item.description: UEFA says it is considering legal action against FIFA president Gianni Infantino and others involved in the now-withdrawn plan to sell a stake in the World Cup to American private equity interests. Infantino shelved the plans after a threatened boycott of FIFA competitions by three of the six football confederations. And now there are calls for him to step down, with a number of candidates, including the Canadian Victor Montagliani, emerging to challenge him in a leadership battle.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24
